result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B gives a consistent token set with rem breakpoints and clamped gutters. Its article grid keeps prose at the measure while code and tables break out to 960px and scroll inside the block, and it states that content stops growing at 1280px. A is solid and a little leaner, but its table says pricing goes to 3 columns at 900px while its CSS waits until 1200px, and `.grid-12` is defined without any column spans. B adds a docs sidebar the request never mentioned, but it is a reasonable addition for a docs site. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A defines one set of tokens (fluid clamp() gutters and gaps, a 68ch measure, 960px breakout for wide blocks, 1280px cap), and its CSS matches the numbers it states. Code and tables scroll inside the block on narrow screens. Its explicit pricing columns avoid an orphaned tier. B is solid, but it contradicts itself on pricing: the table says 3 columns at 900px while the CSS switches at 1200px. It also adds a 12-column grid it barely uses and needs a renderer change to wrap tables.
